issues.description: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service complects identity with value — a frame (immutable fact) now carries a live mutable processor reference
issues.detail: The frame is a value: a piece of data representing the fact 'please re-emit metadata.' By making service a FrameProcessor (a live identity with state, behavior, and a place in the pipeline), the frame is no longer just a value — it's a value tangled with an identity reference. Equality, serialization, logging, and replay all become surprising. A service identifier (string name, id, or even type) would keep the frame as data and let the switcher resolve identity at the edge, where identity actually lives.

issues.description: Targeting is enforced at the consumer, not encoded in routing — the frame is broadcast and then filtered
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcher.process_frame queues the frame to the specific service it wants to talk to, then ServiceSwitcher.push_frame inspects the frame on the way out and decides to suppress it based on equality with active_service. That's two different mechanisms doing the same job: addressing (queue_frame to service) and filtering (isinstance + equality on egress). The 'service' field is doing identity comparison work that the queue_frame call already accomplished. Either route by address or broadcast and filter — doing both is complecting two models of dispatch.

issues.description: Behavior change from 'consume' to 'push downstream after handling' is undocumented in terms of who depends on seeing the frame
issues.detail: Previously RequestMetadataFrame was internal to the switcher and consumed. Now STTService and the mock push it downstream after handling, and the switcher only suppresses it when frame.service matches the active service. That means an inactive service inside a switcher would, if it received the frame, also push it downstream — and the switcher would let it through (frame.service != active_service). The contract 'this frame is internal to the switcher' has been replaced with 'this frame may escape the switcher under conditions X' without naming who downstream is supposed to do with it. State the time semantics and the audience explicitly, or keep it strictly internal.

issues.description: Forward-reference string 'FrameProcessor' on a frame field hints the dependency is going the wrong way
issues.detail: frames.py needing a forward reference to FrameProcessor to describe a data field is a small smell that data is reaching up into the processor layer. Frames are meant to be the values that flow between processors; when a frame's type signature names a processor, the layering has inverted. A typed service-identifier (str, enum, or a small ServiceRef value) would let frames.py stay a leaf module of pure data.

issues.description: Rename adds specificity but the name now leaks the requester's identity into the frame's name
issues.detail: ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame names the producer (ServiceSwitcher) in the type. If another component ever wants to request metadata re-emission, it must either reuse a frame named after a different component or invent a parallel frame. A name describing what the frame asks for (RequestServiceMetadataFrame) keeps the value decoupled from the identity of whoever sends it.

review.summary: The rename and the addition of a target field are reasonable instincts — the old broadcast-and-block model was indeed too coarse. But the chosen shape complects a value (the frame, a fact about what's being requested) with an identity (a live FrameProcessor reference), and then does the targeting work twice: once via queue_frame addressing and again via equality filtering on egress. The simple decomposition is: keep the frame as pure data carrying a service identifier (string/enum/id), let queue_frame do addressing, and let push_frame either always suppress this internal frame or never see it. The question that should have been asked first: is this frame a value that flows through the pipeline, or a message addressed to one processor — and if it's the latter, why is it a Frame at all rather than a direct method call on the target service?
